subject: MSA + Order Form: proposal on liability structure and carve-outs
messages:
From: Tom Sanders <procurement@acmecorp.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmecorp.com>, contracts@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:21:00 +0000
Subject: MSA/Order Form — liability cap and carve-outs

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the draft MSA. Attached is Acme's preferred redline (acme_msa_redline.pdf). Two items we need clarity on before legal signs off:

1) Liability cap basis — Acme prefers an annualized cap tied to fees paid (12-month lookback) so that liability scales as usage grows.
2) Carve-outs — we need explicit carve-outs for IP indemnity, confidentiality breaches, and regulatory fines. We'd like data-breach liability to be uncapped for direct damages, or at least excluded from the cap.

Can Redwood propose final language for: (a) a cap structure (annualized v. total contract amount) and (b) a clean list of carve-outs? We're trying to close by end of month.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Tom Sanders
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

Attachment: acme_msa_redline.pdf (PDF, 412KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Sanders <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmecorp.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form — liability cap and carve-outs

Tom — thanks, received the redline. Looping in Laura and Sergio to finalize. Quick summary of Redwood's starting position and options:

1) Standard Redwood position (preferred): total liability capped at the greater of $1,000,000 or 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (rolling 12 months).
   - Pros: limits our long-tail exposure while aligning with actual consideration exchanged.
   - Cons: may feel less predictable for customers that expect a fixed ceiling.

2) Annualized cap (customer-favored): cap equals fees paid in the prior 12 months (12-month lookback), optionally with a one-time first-term uplift (e.g., 2x for the initial 12 months) to provide ramp protection.
   - Pros: scales with usage and is easier for customers to reason about month-to-month.
   - Cons: can increase our exposure on high-growth accounts.

3) Total-contract cap: cap equals total fees under the order form (not recommended for multi-year, high-usage deals).

Carve-outs we can accept in principle: IP indemnity, willful misconduct/fraud, regulatory fines/penalties, and obligations to process data under law enforcement requests. For data security incidents we prefer a dedicated limit (e.g., a separate cyber-liability bucket) rather than making it fully uncapped.

I'll ask Legal to draft suggested redline language for both options 1 and 2 so you can pick. Laura — can you prepare two short redlines (one for the 2x-or-1M approach and one for the annualized fees approach) plus a recommended single-sentence carve-out list? Sergio/Jordan — any commercial trade-offs we should consider when presenting these options to Acme?

If you prefer to lock in today, we can propose the annualized option with a first-term 2x uplift as a one-time concession and offer a 6-month review clause.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Legal, Contracts (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form — liability cap and carve-outs (redlines attached)

Irene — drafted two concise redlines and a short explainer. See attached (redwood_counter_redlines.docx) and the quick summary below. Legal's recommended compromise:

A) Cap language (preferred legal drafting):
   "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Redwood for all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) an amount equal to two (2) times the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim."

B) Carve-outs (clean list to include in the MSA):
   - Claims arising from Redwood's indemnification obligations for third-party IP infringement;
   - Customer's liability for its own data processing obligations and regulatory penalties;
   - Claims resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence;
   - Liability for breaches of confidentiality obligations (subject to separate confidentiality clause);
   - Any statutory consumer protections that cannot be waived.

C) Data security incidents: propose a dedicated cyber-liability cap (e.g., $2,000,000) with clear definitions for "direct damages" — Legal does not recommend fully uncapped data-breach exposure.

D) Annualized vs total: legal prefers the rolling 12-month lookback tied to fees (gives a clearer link to consideration) rather than total contract value for long-duration, high-usage agreements.

If Sales wants a commercial concession, we can present the first-term uplift (2x) or a credit/discount instead of increasing the permanent cap.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_counter_redlines.docx (Word, 98KB)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form — liability cap and carve-outs (commercial view)

Team — quick commercial note from the field: Acme is timeline-sensitive and is pushing for the annualized cap language. If we hold firm on the 2x-or-1M total cap they may ask for a pricing concession or extended onboarding credits. Two options I think are reasonable:

1) Offer annualized cap (fees in prior 12 months) + first-term uplift to 2x for the initial 12 months only. Combine with a 6-month joint review clause and a technical SLO uplift to reassure them.

2) Keep legal's 2x-of-fees approach but offer $150k of implementation credit or a 3-month free technical onboarding as a concession.

Preference: Option 1 — simpler to explain to Acme procurement and dovetails with their internal accounting. Laura, can you confirm whether Option 1 is acceptable from a risk perspective if we cap data-breach exposure at a separate cyber limit?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Sanders <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmecorp.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form — liability cap and carve-outs

Tom — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. To keep momentum and address Acme's preference for an annualized approach, Redwood can proceed with the following compromise:

1) Liability cap: aggregate liability will be capped at the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) an amount equal to the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim (i.e., an annualized/rolling 12-month lookback).

2) First-term concession: for the initial twelve (12) months following execution, Redwood will increase the cap to the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) two (2) times Fees paid by Customer in the prior 12 months (a one-time uplift).

3) Carve-outs: agreed carve-outs will include IP indemnity, willful misconduct/gross negligence, confidentiality breaches, and statutory consumer protections. For data-security incidents, Redwood will accept a separate cyber-liability bucket capped at $2,000,000 (defined for direct damages only). Regulatory fines/penalties remain excluded from Redwood's indemnity obligations but Customer remains responsible for penalties arising from its own processing obligations.

4) Operational commitments: include a 6-month joint review clause to revisit cap after initial term and a promise to maintain the security controls listed in Schedule 2.

Next steps: Laura will prepare a redline of the MSA incorporating the language above and submit via DocuSign. Sergio/Jordan will offer a brief concession note (implementation credits) if needed during commercial negotiations. Please expect the redline by COB Monday.

If that is acceptable to Acme, please confirm and we'll move to DocuSign. Happy to hop on a short call if you'd like to iron out any remaining points.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Legal, Contracts (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Liability_Options_v2.pdf (PDF, 64KB)
